also: what do you mean by that?

terms.gloss: mean, signify (of a word or a sign)
evidence: Cic. Tusc. 1.88: carēre igitur hoc significat: egēre eō quod habēre velīs
terms.comment: With the word or sign as subject: Quid hoc verbum significat? Lewis & Short: of words, “to mean, import, signify”.

terms.gloss: of a word: mean, have the force of
evidence: Cic. Off. 3.39: hoc verbum quid valeat, nōn vident
Cic. Fin. 2.13: quaerimus verbum Latīnum pār Graecō et quod idem valeat
terms.comment: Idem valet: it means the same.

terms.gloss: what does it mean? (of words, things and doings)
evidence: Ter. Heaut. 615: Quid volt sibi, Syre, haec ōrātiō?
Cic. Sen. 65: avāritia vērō senīlis quid sibi velit, nōn intellegō
terms.comment: From sibi velle, “want for oneself”; of a person, “what is he after?” (see mean, intend).

evidence: Cic. Leg. 3.1 (Lewis & Short): Platōnem vidēlicet dīcis
terms.comment: Of the speaker: Quem dīcis?, “Who do you mean?” Lewis & Short: “to mean so and so”.

evidence: Varr. LL 9.40; Cic. Part. Or. 108; Quint. 9.1.4 (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Also vīs, the force of a word (M-O). Sēnsus for the sense of a word is poetic and post-Augustan (Ov., Quint.).

terms.gloss: what do you mean by that? (what kind of word is that?)
terms.grammar: question: istuc with the partitive genitive verbī
evidence: Plaut. Curc. 1.1.32: quid istuc est verbī? (Lewis & Short s.v. istic)
Traupman 103: what do you mean by that?, quid istuc est verbī?
terms.comment: Literally “what of a word is that?”: asked of a remark that puzzles or offends.

phrases.latin: Quid volt sibi, Syre, haec ōrātiō?
phrases.english: What does this talk mean, Syrus?

phrases.latin: carēre igitur hoc significat: egēre eō quod habēre velīs
phrases.english: So “to lack” means this: to be without what you would like to have.

phrases.latin: plēraque sunt vocābula quibus vulgō ūtimur, neque tamen liquidō scīmus quid ea propriē atque vērē significent
phrases.english: There are many words we use every day without knowing clearly what they properly and truly mean.
